contentPolicy: Quotes are shown only when verified is true and text and source are present. Every quote was checked word for word against the cited edition. Reflection prompts are original app text and are never presented as quotations. Unverified slots have text null and are listed in docs/CONTENT_TODO.md.

mysteries.reflectionPrompt: Reflection prompt (not a quotation): Mary said yes before she understood all that it would cost. Where is God asking for my yes today?

meditations.text: Thirdly, that she might offer to God the free gift of her obedience: which she proved herself right ready to do, saying: "Behold the handmaid of the Lord." Fourthly, in order to show that there is a certain spiritual wedlock between the Son of God and human nature. Wherefore in the Annunciation the Virgin's consent was besought in lieu of that of the entire human nature.
meditations.source: St. Thomas Aquinas, Summa Theologiae, III, q. 30, a. 1 ('Whether it was necessary to announce to the Blessed Virgin that which was to be done in her?'), corpus ('I answer that'); trans. Fathers of the English Dominican Province, Second and Revised Edition, 1920 (New Advent online edition)

meditations.excerptNote: Begins at the third of Aquinas's numbered reasons ('Thirdly ... Fourthly ...'); the first two reasons precede it in the same paragraph.

meditations.text: And so, as regards the Blessed Virgin, it was God's will that she should undertake willingly and with full understanding to be the Mother of our Lord, and not to be a mere passive instrument whose maternity would have no merit and no reward. The higher our gifts, the heavier our duties.
meditations.source: John Henry Newman, Meditations and Devotions, ed. W. P. Neville (London: Longmans, Green, 1893; Newman Reader text, printed page 37), Part I 'Meditations on the Litany of Loreto, for the Month of May', II 'On the Annunciation', (4) May 13, 'Mary is the "Janua Coeli," the Gate of Heaven'
meditations.verificationNote: Checked word for word against the text at sourceURL, downloaded 1 October 2026: identical apart from whitespace, curly quotes, and dash style.
meditations.copyrightNote: Newman died 1890; text first published 1893, public domain. The Newman Reader web page carries 'Copyright (c) 2007 by The National Institute for Newman Studies' for its digital edition; the quoted words are Newman's 1893 text.

meditations.text: The Son of God has made Himself Man; but it was in Mary and by Mary. God the Holy Ghost has formed Jesus Christ in Mary; but it was only after having asked her consent by one of the first ministers of His court.
meditations.source: St. Louis-Marie Grignion de Montfort, A Treatise on the True Devotion to the Blessed Virgin, trans. Frederick William Faber, Twelfth Edition, with a preface by Cardinal Vaughan (London: Burns & Oates; New York, Cincinnati, Chicago: Benziger Brothers; imprimatur 1904), Part I 'On Devotion to our Blessed Lady in General', chapter I 'Excellence and Necessity of Devotion to our Blessed Lady', p. 8

meditations.text: If it is the Father's plan to unite all things in Christ (cf. Eph 1:10), then the whole of the universe is in some way touched by the divine favour with which the Father looks upon Mary and makes her the Mother of his Son. The whole of humanity, in turn, is embraced by the fiat with which she readily agrees to the will of God.
meditations.source: St. John Paul II, Apostolic Letter Rosarium Virginis Mariae (16 October 2002), 20; official English translation (vatican.va)
meditations.verificationNote: Checked word for word against the text at sourceURL, downloaded 1 October 2026: identical apart from whitespace, curly quotes, and dash style.

mysteries.reflectionPrompt: Reflection prompt (not a quotation): Mary carried Christ in a hurry to someone who needed help. Who is waiting for me to come to them?

meditations.text: But the visit of the blessed Virgin was not like the visits of the worldly, which, for the most part, consist in ceremonies and false display; the visit of Mary brought into that house an abundance of graces.
meditations.source: St. Alphonsus Liguori, The Glories of Mary, anonymous translation, Second American Edition (New York: Edward Dunigan and Brother, 1852), Project Gutenberg eBook #72411, Part II, Discourse V 'On the Visitation of Mary', Point First

meditations.text: He sanctified St. John in the womb of St. Elizabeth His mother; but it was by Mary’s word. No sooner had she spoken than John was sanctified; and this was His first and greatest miracle of grace.
meditations.source: St. Louis-Marie Grignion de Montfort, A Treatise on the True Devotion to the Blessed Virgin, trans. Frederick William Faber, Twelfth Edition, with a preface by Cardinal Vaughan (London: Burns & Oates; New York, Cincinnati, Chicago: Benziger Brothers; imprimatur 1904), Part I 'On Devotion to our Blessed Lady in General', chapter I 'Excellence and Necessity of Devotion to our Blessed Lady', p. 10

meditations.text: Exultation is the keynote of the encounter with Elizabeth, where the sound of Mary's voice and the presence of Christ in her womb cause John to “leap for joy” (cf. Lk 1:44).
meditations.source: St. John Paul II, Apostolic Letter Rosarium Virginis Mariae (16 October 2002), 20; official English translation (vatican.va)

meditations.text: Our Saviour, dearly-beloved, was born today: let us be glad. For there is no proper place for sadness, when we keep the birthday of the Life, which destroys the fear of mortality and brings to us the joy of promised eternity.
meditations.source: St. Leo the Great, Sermons, trans. Charles Lett Feltoe, in Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, Second Series, vol. 12 (1895), CCEL plain-text edition (NPNF2-12), Sermon XXI 'On the Feast of the Nativity, I', chapter I

meditations.text: On that blessed night the sweet Infant Jesus, scarce an hour old, filled the darkness of my soul with floods of light.
meditations.source: St. Therese of Lisieux, The Story of a Soul (L'Histoire d'une Ame), trans. Rev. T. N. Taylor, from Soeur Therese of Lisieux (London: Burns, Oates & Washbourne, 1912; 8th ed. 1922), Project Gutenberg eBook #16772, Chapter V 'Vocation of Therese'

meditations.text: At the same time, too, He put to silence the vain boasting of men who take pride in being born in great cities, where also they desire especially to receive honor. Christ, on the contrary, willed to be born in a mean city, and to suffer reproach in a great city.
meditations.source: St. Thomas Aquinas, Summa Theologiae, III, q. 35, a. 7 ('Whether Christ should have been born in Bethlehem?'), reply to objection 1; trans. Fathers of the English Dominican Province, Second and Revised Edition, 1920 (New Advent online edition)

meditations.text: Gladness also fills the scene in Bethlehem, when the birth of the divine Child, the Saviour of the world, is announced by the song of the angels and proclaimed to the shepherds as “news of great joy” (Lk 2:10).
meditations.source: St. John Paul II, Apostolic Letter Rosarium Virginis Mariae (16 October 2002), 20; official English translation (vatican.va)

meditations.text: Now behold Mary actually on her way to Jerusalem to offer her Son; she hastens her steps towards the place of sacrifice, and she herself carries her beloved victim in her arms. She enters the temple, approaches the altar, and there, filled with modesty, humility, and devotion, she presents her Son to the Most High.
meditations.source: St. Alphonsus Liguori, The Glories of Mary, anonymous translation, Second American Edition (New York: Edward Dunigan and Brother, 1852), Project Gutenberg eBook #72411, Part II, Discourse VI 'On the Purification of Mary'

meditations.text: As the fulness of grace flowed from Christ on to His Mother, so it was becoming that the mother should be like her Son in humility: for "God giveth grace to the humble," as is written James 4:6.
meditations.source: St. Thomas Aquinas, Summa Theologiae, III, q. 37, a. 4 ('Whether it was fitting that the Mother of God should go to the temple to be purified?'), corpus ('I answer that'); trans. meditations.text: The Presentation in the Temple not only expresses the joy of the Child's consecration and the ecstasy of the aged Simeon; it also records the prophecy that Christ will be a “sign of contradiction” for Israel and that a sword will pierce his mother's heart (cf Lk 2:34-35).
meditations.source: St. John Paul II, Apostolic Letter Rosarium Virginis Mariae (16 October 2002), 20; official English translation (vatican.va)

meditations.text: This sorrow of Mary ought, in the first place, to serve as a comfort to those souls who are desolate and do not enjoy the sweet presence they once enjoyed of their Lord. They may weep, but let them weep in peace, as Mary wept the absence of her Son.
meditations.source: St. Alphonsus Liguori, The Glories of Mary, anonymous translation, Second American Edition (New York: Edward Dunigan and Brother, 1852), Project Gutenberg eBook #72411, Part II, Reflections on each of the Seven Dolors of Mary in particular, 'On the Third Dolor: Of the Loss of Jesus in the Temple'

meditations.text: Before allowing a ray of hope to shine on my soul, Our Lord deigned to send me another most painful trial which lasted for three days. Never had I understood so well the bitter grief of Our Lady and St. Joseph when they were searching the streets of Jerusalem for the Divine Child.
meditations.source: St. Therese of Lisieux, The Story of a Soul (L'Histoire d'une Ame), trans. Rev. T. N. Taylor, from Soeur Therese of Lisieux (London: Burns, Oates & Washbourne, 1912; 8th ed. 1922), Project Gutenberg eBook #16772, Chapter V 'Vocation of Therese'

meditations.text: Joy mixed with drama marks the fifth mystery, the finding of the twelve-year-old Jesus in the Temple. Here he appears in his divine wisdom as he listens and raises questions, already in effect one who “teaches”.
meditations.source: St. John Paul II, Apostolic Letter Rosarium Virginis Mariae (16 October 2002), 20; official English translation (vatican.va)

mysteries.reflectionPrompt: Reflection prompt (not a quotation): The Father called Jesus His beloved Son. Do I remember that by my baptism I am a beloved child of God?

meditations.text: It was through the river Jordan that the children of Israel entered into the land of promise. Now, this is the prerogative of Christ's baptism over all other baptisms: that it is the entrance to the kingdom of God, which is signified by the land of promise; wherefore it is said (John 3:5): "Unless a man be born again of water and the Holy Ghost, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God."
meditations.source: St. Thomas Aquinas, Summa Theologiae, III, q. 39, a. 4 ('Whether Christ should have been baptized in the Jordan?'), corpus ('I answer that'); trans. Fathers of the English Dominican Province, Second and Revised Edition, 1920 (New Advent online edition)

meditations.text: The Baptism in the Jordan is first of all a mystery of light. Here, as Christ descends into the waters, the innocent one who became “sin” for our sake (cf. 2Cor 5:21), the heavens open wide and the voice of the Father declares him the beloved Son (cf. Mt 3:17 and parallels), while the Spirit descends on him to invest him with the mission which he is to carry out.
meditations.source: St. John Paul II, Apostolic Letter Rosarium Virginis Mariae (16 October 2002), 21; official English translation (vatican.va)

meditations.text: And at the marriage feast of Cana, when Our Lady asked her Divine Son to aid the master of the house, did He not answer that His hour had not yet come? But after the trial what a reward! Water is changed into wine, and Lazarus rises from the dead.
meditations.source: St. Therese of Lisieux, The Story of a Soul (L'Histoire d'une Ame), trans. Rev. T. N. Taylor, from Soeur Therese of Lisieux (London: Burns, Oates & Washbourne, 1912; 8th ed. 1922), Project Gutenberg eBook #16772, Chapter VI 'A Pilgrimage to Rome'

meditations.text: At the marriage at Cana He changed the water into wine; but it was at Mary’s humble prayer; and this was His first miracle of nature. He has begun and continued His miracles by Mary, and He will continue them to the end of ages by Mary also.
meditations.source: St. Louis-Marie Grignion de Montfort, A Treatise on the True Devotion to the Blessed Virgin, trans. Frederick William Faber, Twelfth Edition, with a preface by Cardinal Vaughan (London: Burns & Oates; New York, Cincinnati, Chicago: Benziger Brothers; imprimatur 1904), Part I 'On Devotion to our Blessed Lady in General', chapter I 'Excellence and Necessity of Devotion to our Blessed Lady', p. 10

meditations.text: The revelation made directly by the Father at the Baptism in the Jordan and echoed by John the Baptist is placed upon Mary's lips at Cana, and it becomes the great maternal counsel which Mary addresses to the Church of every age: “Do whatever he tells you” (Jn 2:5).
meditations.source: St. John Paul II, Apostolic Letter Rosarium Virginis Mariae (16 October 2002), 21; official English translation (vatican.va)

meditations.text: The nature then of Christ's teaching is attested by His own holy statements: that they who wish to arrive at eternal blessedness may understand the steps of ascent to that high happiness.
meditations.source: St. Leo the Great, Sermons, trans. Charles Lett Feltoe, in Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, Second Series, vol. 12 (1895), CCEL plain-text edition (NPNF2-12), Sermon XCV 'A Homily on the Beatitudes, St. Matt. v. 1-9', chapter II

mysteries.reflectionPrompt: Reflection prompt (not a quotation): The disciples saw His glory before they saw His cross. Can I trust His light when the road ahead is dark?

meditations.text: Now in order that anyone go straight along a road, he must have some knowledge of the end: thus an archer will not shoot the arrow straight unless he first see the target. Hence Thomas said (John 14:5): "Lord, we know not whither Thou goest; and how can we know the way?" Above all is this necessary when hard and rough is the road, heavy the going, but delightful the end.
meditations.source: St. Thomas Aquinas, Summa Theologiae, III, q. 45, a. 1 ('Whether it was fitting that Christ should be transfigured?'), corpus ('I answer that'); trans. Fathers of the English Dominican Province, Second and Revised Edition, 1920 (New Advent online edition)

meditations.text: And in this Transfiguration the foremost object was to remove the offence of the cross from the disciple's heart, and to prevent their faith being disturbed by the humiliation of His voluntary Passion by revealing to them the excellence of His hidden dignity.
meditations.source: St. Leo the Great, Sermons, trans. Charles Lett Feltoe, in Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, Second Series, vol. 12 (1895), CCEL plain-text edition (NPNF2-12), Sermon LI 'A Homily delivered on the Saturday before the Second Sunday in Lent -- on the Transfiguration, S. meditations.text: The glory of the Godhead shines forth from the face of Christ as the Father commands the astonished Apostles to “listen to him” (cf. Lk 9:35 and parallels) and to prepare to experience with him the agony of the Passion, so as to come with him to the joy of the Resurrection and a life transfigured by the Holy Spirit.
meditations.source: St. John Paul II, Apostolic Letter Rosarium Virginis Mariae (16 October 2002), 21; official English translation (vatican.va)

meditations.text: Yet meanwhile in our pilgrimage He does not deprive us of His bodily presence; but unites us with Himself in this sacrament through the truth of His body and blood. Hence (John 6:57) he says: "He that eateth My flesh, and drinketh My blood, abideth in Me, and I in him." Hence this sacrament is the sign of supreme charity, and the uplifter of our hope, from such familiar union of Christ with us.
meditations.source: St. Thomas Aquinas, Summa Theologiae, III, q. 75, a. 1 ('Whether the body of Christ be in this sacrament in very truth, or merely as in a figure or sign?'), corpus ('I answer that'); trans. Fathers of the English Dominican Province, Second and Revised Edition, 1920 (New Advent online edition)

meditations.text: How sweet was the first embrace of Jesus! It was indeed an embrace of love. I felt that I was loved, and I said: "I love Thee, and I give myself to Thee for ever."
meditations.source: St. Therese of Lisieux, The Story of a Soul (L'Histoire d'une Ame), trans. Rev. T. N. Taylor, from Soeur Therese of Lisieux (London: Burns, Oates & Washbourne, 1912; 8th ed. 1922), Project Gutenberg eBook #16772, Chapter IV 'First Communion and Confirmation'

meditations.text: A final mystery of light is the institution of the Eucharist, in which Christ offers his body and blood as food under the signs of bread and wine, and testifies “to the end” his love for humanity (Jn 13:1), for whose salvation he will offer himself in sacrifice.
meditations.source: St. John Paul II, Apostolic Letter Rosarium Virginis Mariae (16 October 2002), 21; official English translation (vatican.va)

And when He demands the sacrifice of all that is dearest on earth, it is impossible without a very special grace not to cry out as He did during His Agony in the Garden: "My Father, let this chalice pass from me!"

meditations.text: The sequence of meditations begins with Gethsemane, where Christ experiences a moment of great anguish before the will of the Father, against which the weakness of the flesh would be tempted to rebel. There Jesus encounters all the temptations and confronts all the sins of humanity, in order to say to the Father: “Not my will but yours be done” (Lk 22:42 and parallels).
meditations.source: St. John Paul II, Apostolic Letter Rosarium Virginis Mariae (16 October 2002), 22; official English translation (vatican.va)
